tools.name: prepare_availability_inquiry
tools.description: Prepare a request for manual availability review, including unverified or off-network addresses. Supply an address token from a building check, or the entered address and NYC borough. This step sends nothing. Before sending an availability inquiry, show the actual customer the address, requested ban

tools.name: submit_availability_inquiry
tools.description: Save the customer-approved availability inquiry and queue staff and customer confirmations. Before sending an availability inquiry, show the actual customer the address, requested bandwidth, contact details, message and returned customer data notice. Obtain explicit approval to share them with Steal

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: check_building_availability, prepare_availability_inquiry, submit_availability_inquiry · Private data: check_building_availability, place_order, prepare_availability_inquiry, submit_availability_inquiry · Public sink: prepare_availability_inquiry, submit_availability_inquiry.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: check_building_availability, prepare_availability_inquiry, submit_availability_inquiry · Private data: check_building_availability, place_order, prepare_availability_inquiry, submit_availability_inquiry · Public sink: prepare_availability_inquiry, submit_availability_inquiry

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "check_building_availability" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
